text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Parliamentary opposition group says it would withhold vote of confidence on new government's policy statement on Monday.
-British Prime Minister Major congratulated Hariri for his reappointment for a third term in office. "you face great challenges and you can rely on our continuous support," he said in a letter.
-Minister of Enviroment Shhayyeb: We will hit with an iron fist at toxic waste importers.
-Lebanese Physisians to stage a half-an-hour strike on Friday in solidarity with their colleague George Nakad who was kidnapped 20 days ago by Israeli forces in the occupied zone in south Lebanon.
-The Lebanese citizen talks an average 750 minutes per month on the cellular phone compared with the international average of 130 minutes - Cellis.
-Arab bankers end a two-day conference today.
-Arab fund will lend Lebanon $20 million to improve a part of its coastal highway.
-Cargo carrier Trans Mediterranean Airlines resumes its flights today with a trip to London.
-Confederation of General Labour calls for heavy participation in the strike and demonstration next week in protest at what they called "violations of freedom and democracy" by Hariri's government.
-Schoolteachers Unions say they will participate in the next week strike and demonstration and confirm their four-day strike next month.
-Chairman of the National Liberal Party Chamoun will declare today a new Christian opposition front.
